page.overview:
Who is William Blake?

William Blake is a recurrent character in the works of British author David Hambling, and the primary focus of a story cycle to which he lends his name.

Born in the early 20th century, by the 1920s Blake was one of the Bright Young Things, a term given to the post-World War I generation of the London party scene. While studying for his PhD, he made a living by tutoring promising lower-achievers, at that time renting a room in the house of an older couple by the name of Hall (: "The Dulwich Horror of 1927").

Blake was never to finish his degree, however, as a result of an encounter with an extra-dimensional entity; the same encounter left him with near-fatal injuries, killing most of his friends and putting the two other survivors forever beyond his reach (: "The Dulwich Horror of 1927").

Later in life, Blake would become a teacher, living a semi-itinerant life and moving regularly in an effort to leave his past behind him (: "The Monsters in the Park").
